title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: Meeting tech issues steal 16 minutes from productivity each time they happen
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**YOUR WORKPLACE IS ON MUTE**


Tech issues cost businesses 16 minutes of lost productivity each time they happen, based on new Harris Poll research with[Logitech](https://theharrispoll.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/workplace-equation-2026.pdf) .


- 71% of employees say they experience technology issues “sometimes” and 30% “very often.”
- 30% of leaders say meeting tech issues cost their organization 16 minutes each occurrence.
- Only 27% of organizations treat the “workplace experience” as a core business strategy.
- 81% of HR leaders say they are responsible for the workplace experience, followed by IT (76%) and real estate/facilities (72%).
- 89% of leaders say being in the office provides experiences employees cannot achieve at home or somewhere else.
- The primary drivers for coming into the office are changing: to attend meetings (46% today and expected to fall to 35% in the future), to connect with colleagues (39% today, growing to 42% in the future), policy requirement (29% today, 23% future), training (27% today, 31% future) and to use specialized spaces like labs and 3-D printing (23% today, 33% future).
- 24% of organizations bring IT and AV teams into a project before office space planning begins.
- 32% of companies update office layouts or technology standards continuously, based on live usage data.
- *See also:[72% of Tech Decision-Makers Feel AI Initiatives Today Are Falling Short](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/new-survey-from-collibra-by-the-harris-poll-finds-72-of-tech-decision-makers-feel-ai-initiatives-today-are-falling-short-302879680.html)*


**YOUTH SPORTS BREAKING THE BUDGET**


Two-thirds of parents with children under 18 are considering pulling them out of youth sports due to the escalating costs, based on the new[Good Sports](https://www.goodsports.org/the-cost-of-play-index/) Cost of Play Index, conducted by The Harris Poll.


- 68% of parents of kids considered pulling them out of sports.
- Unsustainable costs are the top reason among 26% of parents – even among households with annual income of more than $100,000.
- Other factors include injury concerns (24%), poor coaching (23%), child does not enjoy it (23%) and a negative team environment (22%).
- 80% of parents say their children are currently playing sports compared with 84% in 2024.
- 53% of parents worry they will not be able to afford sports for their child next year.
- 77% say the growth of private clubs and travel teams is pricing many children out of participation.
- 67% say there has been a decrease in low-cost or public-school youth sports opportunities during the last five years.
- 56% say there are not enough viable recreational or intramural youth sports options available locally.


**SCHOOL NEEDS A RESET**


Teens, parents and teachers see a growing relevance gap in schools, and students want learning tied to their future goals, according to The Relevance Gap Study from Harris Poll and[MilkPEP](https://theharrispoll.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/The-Relevance-Gap-Study-Milk-x-The-Harris-Poll-9.11.pdf) .


- 82% of teachers report declining student attentiveness.
- 55% of students disengage when subjects feel irrelevant to their future, and most (97%) are less engaged when lessons do not align with personal goals.
- 53% rank financial literacy, stock market knowledge or crypto among what they most want to learn, followed by entrepreneurship (45%), wellness (44%) and day-to-day skills (44%).
- Half of students say social media is more relevant to their aspirations than school, and 45% trust online experts and creators for goal-aligned information.
- 69% use YouTube several times a week to learn, followed by TikTok (57%) and Instagram (53%).


**READY TO VOTE, WAITING TO BE HEARD**


Young Americans are increasingly ready to vote, volunteer and lead, yet most believe elected officials are not listening to them, according to our Harris Poll research with[UNICEF USA](https://www.unicefusa.org/sites/default/files/2026-09/Harris%20Poll%20-%20Policymakers%20-%202026.pdf) .


- State-election voting intent is up 15 points among young people since 2024, with local-election participation also on the rise.
- 82% say young people can make a difference, and 74% believe their political participation can improve the country.
- Yet only 30% feel included in decisions affecting them, while 63% say elected officials do not value their opinions.
- 62% say local leaders are invested in their future, versus 42% who say the same of federal leaders.
- Cost of living is youth’s top concern (61%) and their leading midterm issue (31%).
- To feel heard, young people want leaders to understand their views (44%), consider them in legislation (43%), hold honest dialogue (42%) and involve them in decisions (42%).
